issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]). In the solution repository Bookstore.swift the initializer is declared as init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) (extra parameter), while the solution's Client calls Bookstore(books: books) (single parameter). This constructor parameter mismatch (and the extra, unexpected parameter in the solution) contradicts the specification and would confuse or block students attempting to instantiate Bookstore as described.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the problem specification by providing init(books: [Book]) (remove the extraneous 'valid: Bool' parameter) or add an overload init(books: [Book]) that forwards to any internal initializer. Ensure all references (e.g. Client.assembleBookstore) use the same initializer signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]), but the solution implementation defines init(books: [Book], valid: Bool). This introduces an unexpected identifier/parameter ('valid') and a mismatched initializer signature, breaking the direct mapping from the exercise requirement to the implementation and causing confusion (and a call-site mismatch where Bookstore(books: books) is used).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Bookstore initializer with the problem statement and template by removing the extra 'valid' parameter and using init(books: [Book]). Alternatively, if a validation flag is required, give it a sensible default (e.g. init(books: [Book], valid: Bool = true)) so calls like Bookstore(books: books) remain valid.
